text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD alert fired — INFERENCE-QUEUE-LATENCY (P1) — tail latency spike >400ms on seq-processing queue (prod). PagerDuty link: <https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD-1738809999>

Sasha: grabbing this, i'm oncall now. starting triage.

Miguel: @Sasha saw it too, my phone blew up. i'm infra oncall, can you take initial? i'll join the bridge in ~2m.

Sasha: taking. acked on PD. will collect dashboards and logs. :eyes:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by Sasha. Escalation timer stopped.

Sasha: quick summary from dashboards: eu-west-1 seq-processing queue shows sustained latency, CPU on pool-inference-gpu-3 at 96%, 99th pct latency ~420ms. 5xx rate is still low. looks like backpressure rather than outright failures. running some live checks:
```bash
# probe healthy pods
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=model-serving -o wide
# tail recent logs for seq-worker
kubectl logs -n prod deploy/seq-worker -c inference --tail=200 | grep "seq" | tail -n 50
```

Priya: any recent deploys? I see a canary rollout for model-serving v2.8 ~15m ago in the deploy history.

Sasha: yes that matches timeline. v2.8 canary got some traffic. candidate for rollback if we confirm regressed latency on long-seq paths.

Miguel: i'll start warming extra replicas on the dedicated pool while you verify. running: `./tools/scale-dedicated --pool seq-proc --replicas 6` — kicked that off a min ago.

Sasha: after scaling, tail latency dropped to ~120ms on average but spikes persist on requests with seq length > 2048. suspect attention kernel regression in v2.8 under long sequences.

Ben: Customer impact check: CS says we got 3 inbound pings in #support from AcmeCorp and BetaApps complaining about slow completions. no errors, just slow. timeline ~8m window.

Anita: can we get request ids / trace ids so CS can correlate?

Ben: pasted ids: trace-7ad3, trace-7ad4, trace-7ad9 (in thread). forwarding to Acme contact now.

Priya: recommendation: isolate canary by scaling canary replicas to 0 and route traffic back to stable v2.7, monitor for 10m. If latency steady, treat as regression.

Sasha: executing isolation: `kubectl scale deploy/model-serving-canary --replicas=0 -n prod`. doing gradual drain. will monitor metrics. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

Miguel: can you confirm K/V cache usage? long sequences might bypass cache and trigger heavier kernels. pulling kv metrics now.

Sasha: KV cache hitrate is unchanged. this looks like execution path change in v2.8 for long sequences. after canary scaled down we're seeing 95th pct ~80ms, 99th ~140ms. good improvement.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by Sasha.

Sasha: marking mitigation: rollback/isolate canary + scale dedicated pool. will leave canary scaled down until perf patch. assigning postmortem to @Priya + @Miguel.

Miguel: i'll collect perf profiles and kernel traces. suspect change in fused-attention path. will diff kernels between v2.7 and v2.8.

Ben: customer comms: I'll send a short note to affected customers: ack, what happened, mitigation, and ETA for follow-up. CS already pinged AcmeCorp.

Sasha: incident duration ~21m from initial page to mitigation. closing bridge in 5. Incident requires postmortem + runbook update for model canary perf gating.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert closed by Sasha. Duration 00:21:01. Postmortem required.

Anita: ack. i'll own overnight watch and follow-ups. leaving a short follow-up TODO: "followup/1738809999 - confirm kernel fallback and add canary perf smoke check to deploy pipeline".

Sasha: thanks all. handing off remaining actions to Anita for the night. ping me if it reappears. :thumbsup: 

Anita: ack — i'll post an update in #incidents in the morning with metrics and any residual anomalies.

Priya: i'll draft the postmortem skeleton and attach Miguel's perf artifacts once available.

Miguel: will upload perf traces and a minimal repro in the repo under `infra/perf/1738809999`.

Ben: will log the customer outreach notes and mark tickets with incident id 1738809999.

Sasha: closing thread. good job team. :wave:
